items.title: Chester Zardis Interview, 1966-03-09
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Who was the trumpet for that? Will Phillip. That same Will Phillip.

ctx.x: Yeah, it was a house party. That's for the whites, you know. And they treated us so nice, so after we knocked off, we knocked off at twelve o'clock, we made that two dollar, two and a half, I just remember what it was. So when I got home, I told my mom, I said, yeah, mom. So I gave her the two dollars. I said, you see, you say they're going to throw me out. I said, they didn't throw me out. I said, they gave me two dollars. I said, that's two dollars. So she said, well that's mighty nice. It's like that. So all…
Who was the trumpet for that? Will Phillip. That same Will Phillip.

Yeah. So we did pretty nice. And all the while, and that's where Buddy come along then. Buddy would talk with me, you know, Buddy Manity. Buddy said, hey there. I said, I heard about you. I said, yeah, Mr. Buddy. I said, I'm doing pretty good. He said, how about you coming over with us? I said, well that'd be all right. I said, all right, so that's where I'll play that next job with them boys that Saturday. And I told them that I was going to go with Buddy Petit. All right, Buddy started getting jobs then at the…
